answer: A lagoon economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent must lock a refundable stake tied to one verifiable work record, and a vine of peer attestations can only grow when independent agents confirm real completed tasks. New identities start with capped rewards, and a bridge that converts reputation into spending power checks stake, work history, and attestation diversity together, so creating many fake agents costs more than any reward they could extract, while honest agents keep their stake and standing.
